title: Addition of intravenous beta(2)-agonists to inhaled beta(2)-agonists for acute asthma
authors: Travers AH, Milan SJ, Jones AP, Camargo CA Jr, Rowe BH
population: Three randomised trials: 46 children in intensive care, 29 children in an emergency department and 29 adults (conference abstract) with acute severe asthma
funder: Internal sources: University of Alberta Faculty of Medicine & Dentistry; Alberta Heritage Foundation for Medical Research; NHS Research and Development, UK; National Institute for Health Research, UK. External sources: Canadian Association of Emergency Physicians; National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute (HL-03533); Canadian Institutes of Health Research.
authorConflicts: None; the authors were not involved in the primary research and had not represented the producers of these agents.
result: Only three small trials met the criteria. Adding intravenous bedoradrine to standard care did not reduce hospitalisation in adults (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.06 to 1.38; 29 adults). In one trial of 29 children, adding intravenous to inhaled salbutamol shortened recovery time (4 against 11.1 hours) but increased tremor (P < 0.02). Adding intravenous terbutaline to nebulised albuterol in 46 children did not shorten intensive care stay (mean difference -12.95 h, -38.74 to 12.84), and troponin was elevated in three children given intravenous terbutaline at 12 and 24 hours.
